title: Machine and Terminal
premise: Tamsin Brightwater is a courier-terraformer tending the Verdance, a garden ship seeded for generations that will never see Earth. When the colony's children begin dreaming one shared dream — a message buried in the old war-relay network — Tamsin discovers his own long-dead mother's voice woven into it, sent before her death decades ago and looping ever since. To deliver it, he must fly the silent corridor between two worlds that each believe the other fired first, knowing the message's truth will indict his own colony's founders. In the end he broadcasts it to both fleets at once: the war dissolves not in victory but in shared grief, and the children's dream finally goes quiet as the garden blooms for the living at last.
about_author: Emrys Nakamura is the pen name of a former hydroponics engineer who spent six years on remote agricultural stations before turning to fiction. Their work blends hard ecological detail with quiet, aching humanism.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. He runs the supply loop between Verdance Station and the relay buoy Halcyon, tending seedlings meant for unborn colonists while nursing his grief for his mother, lost in the war's first strike. Establishes found family among the station crew. Emotional beat: lonely devotion, love expressed through maintenance.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Dream
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Tamsin and nine-year-old Iyo, the gardener's apprentice. The colony's children wake reciting identical fragments — coordinates, a woman's voice. The council dismisses it as mass hysteria; Iyo insists the voice is singing to them. Emotional beat: unease blooming into wonder.

chapters.title: What the Relay Keeps
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At buoy Halcyon he finds the relay's memory core corrupted but active, replaying a transmission older than the war's end. A fragment of the voice matches the children's dream — and matches recordings of his mother, Dr. Sefa Brightwater. Emotional beat: shock curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: Council of Ash
chapters.summary: POV: Councilor Vey, Tamsin's estranged mentor. Vey recognizes the transmission and orders it suppressed; the founders' logs prove Earth's first strike was provoked by Verdance itself. She weighs protecting the colony against burying the truth. Emotional beat: duty tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: Iyo's Map
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Iyo's POV together. The children's shared dream resolves into a route through the silent corridor — the path Sefa flew on her final mission. Tamsin realizes she hid the full message where only someone who loved her would think to look. Emotional beat: found family forming around shared purpose.

chapters.title: The Corridor of No Answer
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, alone aboard the courier. He flies the dead zone between the fleets, dodging automated mines still obeying a war both sides claim to want ended. His ship's AI, grown from Sefa's old code, begins completing her sentences. Emotional beat: terror transfigured by intimacy with the dead.

chapters.title: Earth's Last Loop
chapters.summary: POV: Admiral Okonkwo of the Earth fleet, receiving countdown data — the final transmission loop will overwrite all archives in seventy-two hours. Her intelligence flags an unauthorized courier entering the corridor. She must decide whether to fire. Emotional beat: weariness of command, fear disguised as procedure.

chapters.title: Everything Sefa Buried
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the deep relay he recovers the complete message: proof Verdance's founders triggered the first strike, and Sefa's plea for both sides to stand down, recorded as she died buying time to send it. Grief and fury collide; he nearly turns back. Emotional beat: the cost of truth made flesh.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, rotating POV across Tamsin, Vey, Okonkwo, and Iyo. Tamsin hijacks both fleets' channels and plays everything — the confession, his mother's voice, the children's dream sung live from Verdance. Weapons hold. Vey confesses publicly; Okonkwo stands down her fleet mid-volley. Emotional beat: catharsis through unbearable honesty.

chapters.title: Garden for the Living
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Iyo's POV, one year later. Peace talks proceed slowly; the first Earth ships arrive not as invaders but as pilgrims to the garden. The children's dream has gone quiet, replaced by ordinary dreams. Tamsin plants a tree for his mother among the living rows. Emotional beat: mourning resolved into hope, memory becoming soil.
